newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics off on estimate cuts, Cisco.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics off on estimate cuts, Cisco.

text.p: Shares of U.S. Robotics Corp continued to slide Thursday after analysts cut earnings estimates for the modem maker and Cisco Systems Inc said it would use competitors' technology.
Cisco said it planned to offer high-speed access products using technology from Lucent Technologies Inc and Rockwell International Corp's Rockwell Semiconductor Systems.
"I would say that's probably an excuse to push (U.S. Robotics) down, plus many analysts reduced their numbers," said Amar Senan, an analyst for Volpe, Welty & Co.
Senan said he trimmed his fiscal 1997 earnings estimate for U.S. Robotics to $3.33 a share from $3.46, and cut his fiscal 1998 estimate to $4.24 from $4.43.
He cited expected higher sales, marketing and interest expenses, indicated by the Skokie, Ill.-based company following the release of fiscal first quarter earnings.
However, Senan said U.S. Robotics was in the midst of a transition to high-speed modem technology and he continued to rate the company a strong buy.
He set a 12-month price target of $109 on the stock.

Stephen Levy, an analyst for Oppenheimer & Co, cut his fiscal second quarter estimate by $0.04 a share to $0.78 and his estimate for fiscal 1997 by $0.05 to $3.45. But he also maintained his buy rating on the stock.
Shares of U.S. Robotics closed 4-1/8 lower at 68-1/8.
